# kapsel-cli golden `or-true`. Regenerate with KAPSEL_BLESS=1.
# kapsel -c false || true
--- input
false || true
--- stderr (exit 65)
error[KS-R001]: `|| true` turns any failure of the command before it into success and destroys the error signal; let the command fail, or stop with `|| exit 1`
 --> -c:1:7
  |
1 | false || true
  |       ^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: `|| true` hides the exit status the next step or the caller needs to know the work failed (REQ-KS-012)
  = note: refused alike, judged with the `test` and `exit` code the run uses: a right-hand side of `||` that is `true` or `:` or has one as a pipeline stage; an `exit` that certainly runs with status 0 (`exit 0`, `exit 256`, `exit -0`, `exit " 0"`, a bare `exit` after status 0 or after `echo`/`printf`), also in a loop's condition or body; `!` of something that always fails (`false`, a false or malformed test, `export 1bad`, `X=$(false)`); a `test`/`[` that is true whatever its expansions are (literal words, a quoted expansion next to literal text, `$(false)`, which prints nothing); assignments with no `$(...)`, or whose last `$(...)` always ends with status 0; `export` of valid literal names with quoted values; a `for` loop with no items; a loop whose body never runs or always ends in one of these
  = help: drop the `|| true` and let the command fail, or stop on the failure: `cmd || exit 1`; if the failure is expected, test for its cause first: `test -e stale.lock && rm stale.lock`

error: refused: 1 error
